sn1.25:1.1: “If a bhikkhu is an arahant, Consummate,
sn1.25:1.2: with taints destroyed, One who bears his final body,
sn1.25:1.3: Would he still say, ‘I speak’? And would he say,
sn1.25:2.1: “If a bhikkhu is an arahant, Consummate,
sn1.25:2.2: with taints destroyed, One who bears his final body,
sn1.25:2.4: And he might say, ‘They speak to me.’
sn1.25:2.6: He uses such terms as mere expressions.”
sn1.25:3.1: “When a bhikkhu is an arahant, Consummate,
sn1.25:3.2: with taints destroyed, One who bears his final body,
sn1.25:3.3: Is it because he has come upon conceit
sn1.25:3.4: That he would say, ‘I speak,’ That he would say,
sn1.25:4.1: “No knots exist for one with conceit abandoned;
sn1.25:4.2: For him all knots of conceit are consumed.
sn1.25:4.3: Though the wise one has transcended the conceived,
sn1.25:4.4: He still might say, ‘I speak,’ He might say too,
sn1.25:5.3: He uses such terms as mere expressions.”
